(B) Material improvement directive.

The central objective should be changed from maximin gain to minimax residual variance. Under mutual exclusivity, h(c):=n^-2 tr[Pi^-1 Omega Pi^-1 Q(c)]=h(0)+2c/n, because tr(Pi^-1 Omega Pi^-1 E)=-2n. Hence max_B min_e g_B(c_e) and min_B max_e {h(c_e)-g_B(c_e)} are generally different decisions. The latter is the faithful robust analogue of Zhao's variance-minimizing problem. It also immediately gives weak worst-copula dominance over every zero-covariance optimizer; only strict dominance needs a witness.

Exact D0 directive:

Replace the primary maximin-gain rule by the minimax-residual rule v_mm=min over B in B_kappa of w(B), A_mm=argmin w(B). Do not merely relabel r(B): prove the identity h(c)=h(0)+2c/n, state that maximin gain and minimax residual are not algebraically equivalent when cL<cU, and preferably give a lawful counterexample with different optimizer sets. Prove sup over B in A_mm of w(B) <= inf over B0 in A0 of w(B0) unconditionally; retain the witness only for a positive gap and neighborhood persistence. Port the plug-in theorem to uniform convergence, value consistency, and outer-limit consistency for A_mm. Repair the certified interface by adding Q(cL),Q(cU), equivalently the four marginal moments, and leave the corrected finite-epsilon solver explicitly open.

Results transfer to implementable Zhao bases by representative inclusion, but fixed-kappa global optimality does not transfer upward. Conversely, any nonsingular Zhao optimizer, if it exists, lies in some basis-dependent B_kappa; singular bases and any pseudoinverse interpretation remain uncovered.

The corrected question must concern the minimax-residual correspondence, and a checkable certificate must include the endpoint moment matrices that determine the residual objective.  This narrows the witness obligation to the faithful robust variance decision without assuming the positive gap or regularity slack that the OEQ asks to establish.

changed.from:
The universal certified-solver conclusion is false for the interface \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) as defined.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/10\), the two marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_1,\delta_0)\) produce the same encoded tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their robust values satisfy \(v^\star=0\) and \(v^\star\ge1/3\), respectively.  Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) can always return rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v^\star\le U_{\varepsilon}\) with \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\); hence the conjunction requested in oeq:certified-global-basis does not hold.
changed.to:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.
changed.reason: After the directed repair, the certified interface contains the endpoint moment matrices, so the two old instances no longer have the same encoded input and the universal obstruction as currently worded is false.  The proposed theorem restricts the negative result to the genuinely moment-incomplete input, recomputes the exact minimax-residual values, and explicitly leaves finite termination of the repaired moment-complete solver open.

\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z,

Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
If the right-hand infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
This value transfer concerns only the nonsingular ordinary-inverse projective class \(\mathcal B_Z\), not singular or pseudoinverse bases or Zhao's larger unquotiented domain.

Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B)).
\]
If the middle infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
Thus the fixed-threshold values exhaust the entire maximal well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain in value through the quotient; singular or Moore--Penrose bases remain outside this conclusion.

\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,

=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.

Thus the signed observed stack is already inverse-probability weighted and the formula applies the additional \(\Pi^{-1}\); in particular

\[

=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]

changed.from: The exploratory record \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}\) is the reproducible procedure implemented by \(\texttt{discovery/jiangxi\_robust\_reanalysis.py}\).  It starts from the Cai--de Janvry--Sadoulet replication tables \(\texttt{0422survey.dta}\) and \(\texttt{0422allinforawnet.dta}\), cleans identifiers, sentinel \(99\), self-loops, and duplicate directed nominations while retaining cross-village nominations, constructs Zhao's three target populations for \(\tau_{10},\tau_{21},\tau_{32}\), and uses the disclosed independent Bernoulli \((1/2)\) reconstruction necessitated by the unreleased original strata.  It splits connected components of the exposure-overlap graph without cutting components, estimates the two marginal laws and Fr\'echet endpoints on each training fold, optimizes the robust and zero-covariance bases under the same initialization list and iteration budget, and deploys each held-out basis using def:observable-coefficient-map with the additional \(\Pi^{-1}\) factor.  It is required to report point estimates, design-randomization standard errors, both endpoint losses, worst loss, and numerical optimization gaps.  The AEA download redirected to authenticated access and returned HTTP \(403\) in this solve environment, so no corrected numerical table is asserted.  The protocol is exploratory because its internal cross-fitting is not the independent unpaired pilot of ass:unpaired-pilot.
changed.to: The exploratory record \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}\) is the reproducible but unexecuted procedure implemented by \(\texttt{discovery/jiangxi\_robust\_reanalysis.py}\). The procedure cleans identifiers, sentinel \(99\), self-loops, and duplicate directed nominations while retaining cross-village nominations, constructs the three target populations for \(\tau_{10},\tau_{21},\tau_{32}\), and uses the disclosed independent Bernoulli \((1/2)\) reconstruction necessitated by the unreleased original strata.  It splits connected components of the exposure-overlap graph without cutting components, estimates the two marginal laws and Fr\'echet endpoints on each training fold, and optimizes robust and zero-covariance bases under the same initialization list and iteration budget.  Each held-out basis is deployed through def:observable-coefficient-map with Zhao's ordinary inverse and the additional \(\Pi^{-1}\) factor; no Moore--Penrose safeguard is used or attributed to Zhao. The latter is not a certified upper-minus-lower optimization gap.  The authenticated replication data were unavailable in the solve environment, so the protocol was not executed and no numerical table is asserted.  It remains exploratory because its internal cross-fitting is not the independent unpaired pilot of ass:unpaired-pilot.

For every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), the ordinary-inverse loss has the exact intercept--slope form
\[
w(B)=h(0)-a_B+p_\xi(b_B).
\]
Suppose the ordinary-domain zero-covariance and minimax extrema are attained.  Then
\[
\Delta_Z=
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}
-\left[a^\star-\min_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B)\right].
\]
Consequently strict ordinary-domain improvement holds if and only if \(\Delta_Z>0\), equivalently if and only if there is \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) for which
\[
\min_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C)-p_\xi(b_B)
>a^\star-a_B.
\]
Thus some slope-penalty advantage must strictly exceed the sacrificed zero-covariance gain.  Through \(q_Z\), all displayed values are unchanged on \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), and every attained optimizer correspondence there is exactly the inverse image of its projective correspondence.  No universal strictness, minimax interchange, singular completion, or semidefinite reduction is asserted.

\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  Then
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
n\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly over all arrays with \(0\le Y_i(a)\le1\).  If \(c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\), then the oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H).
\]
Consequently the same ex ante variance for the feasible Horvitz--Thompson-coefficient estimator equals \(\ell_B(c_H)+o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over the rate-admissible class.  The expectations over \(H^{\otimes n}\) in these displays are ex ante basis-performance averages, not additional randomness in the conditional design-based estimand.

\[

and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope

\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}

\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad
e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]

\[

\[

\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu

\right]
-

\right]

\]

\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.

3. Add the new condition as an explicit premise/dependency to lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate, and thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer. Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:frechet-covariance-domain hold and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  For the novel Moore--Penrose completion of def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion,
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)
=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
Define the possibly empty completion equality set
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
Writing \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\) for the fixed-threshold argmin, its rank-two stratum is exactly
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\cap\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\iota\!\left(
\bigcup_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,
\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing,\ 
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+}}
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\right).
\]
In particular, if the ordinary-domain infimum is attained at \(C\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  Conversely, if \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), then \(C\) attains the ordinary-domain infimum and belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa_C)\) for some \(\kappa_C>0\) satisfying \(\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  The singular equality stratum is
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\setminus\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1,\ w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
A singular equality point need not imply attainment on \(\mathcal B_Z\).  No unconditional completion attainment, no singular equality point, and no attribution of the completion to Zhao is asserted.
changed.reason: The current wording inherits an unconditional minimum and minimizer interpretation from the old completion definition, although the Moore--Penrose loss need not be lower semicontinuous across rank drops. The narrowed statement uses the directed infimum definition, treats \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) as a possibly empty equality set, and makes attainment conclusions only for rank-two equality points or an independently attained ordinary infimum.

Suppose ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}
\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|
\le R_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
\left|
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\ell_B(c_H)
\right|
\le R_n.
\]
The oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H),
\qquad
c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}.
\]
Since \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\), one has \(nR_n\to0\); hence the feasible and oracle conditional design variances differ by \(o(n^{-1})\), and the feasible ex ante variance equals \(\ell_B(c_H)+o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over the rate-admissible class.  The expectations over \(H^{\otimes n}\) are ex ante basis-performance averages, not additional randomness in the conditional design-based estimand.

\[

+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments, one also has
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and therefore
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le 2n^{-2}\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

\[

\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments, one also has
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and therefore
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le 2n^{-2}\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence the exact sensitivity condition
\[
nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in }L^1
\]
implies uniform first-order plug-in accuracy for both criteria.  A sufficient bounded-pilot condition is
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

{"id":"lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence","kind":"lemma","statement":"Suppose ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over the nonempty class \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}
\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|
\le R_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
\left|
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\ell_B(c_H)
\right|
\le R_n.
\]
The oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H),
\qquad
c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}.

Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) be the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is defined, and let \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).  Then \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) is surjective, and
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
C=B\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)
\quad\text{for some }t_1t_0\ne0.
\]
For every such diagonal \(T\), every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), and every \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\),
\[
g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
\ell_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=\ell_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
w(q_Z(BT))=w(q_Z(B)).
\]
Consequently, for every nonempty \(K\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\), the infima and suprema of each displayed pullback criterion over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) equal those over \(K\), and every attained argmin or argmax correspondence on the matrix domain is exactly the inverse image under \(q_Z\) of its quotient correspondence. Suppose ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over the nonempty class \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}
\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|
\le R_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
\left|
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\ell_B(c_H)
\right|
\le R_n.
\]
The oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H),
\qquad
c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}.
\]
Since \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\), one has \(nR_n\to0\); hence the feasible and oracle conditional design variances differ by \(o(n^{-1})\), and the feasible ex ante variance equals \(\ell_B(c_H)+o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over the rate-admissible class.  The expectations over \(H^{\otimes n}\) are ex ante basis-performance averages, not additional randomness in the conditional design-based estimand.

\[

+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*

\[

=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad

\]

\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

\le 2n^{-2}\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.

{"id":"thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer","kind":"theorem","statement":"Suppose ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility hold.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces. These selectors and limits are secondary regular rank-two deployment results.  No primitive condition in this theorem proves existence of uniformly bounded \(L_n\); the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion is conditional on the displayed global linear error bound.","free_symbols":["n","v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}","\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}","B","\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}","w(B)","g_B(c)","P","\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}","\widehat B_0","H","\Gamma(F_1,F_0)","F_1","F_0","\nu","Y","\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}","\widehat Q_e","Q(c)","C_n","\widehat w(B)","\widehat g_B(c)"],"depends_on":["ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility","ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence","ass:frechet-covariance-domain","lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate","lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence","thm:fixed-basis-endpoints","def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator","def:gain-loss"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"This theorem derives nonempty measurable pilot selectors, finite pilot-selection regret, and a deterministic feasible-estimator variance bridge before taking the first-order limit.","gap":"The zero-surrogate finite-\(n\) conclusion uses a bounded deterministic linear error bound between nominal-gain regret and worst-loss deficit; outer argmax consistency alone is insufficient on the \(n^{-1}\) scale.","consumer":"prop:ordinary-domain-feasible-ht-gap-transfer"}

{"id":"prop:ordinary-domain-feasible-ht-gap-transfer","kind":"proposition","statement":"Assume ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.  Neither the optimizer-containment condition nor a primitive theorem yielding uniformly bounded \(L_n\) is proved here; both are separate checkable hypotheses. {"id":"lem:triangle-completion-singular-strata-certificate","kind":"lemma","statement":"For the triangle matrices displayed in thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, the rank-zero and rank-one strata induced by Zhao's published unquotiented pseudoinverse carrier and expressed in the note's quotient obey
\[
\sup_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)
=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}
\]
and
\[
\inf_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)
=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
More precisely, rank zero has \(g_B^+(0)=0\) and \(w^+(B)=171/200\).  In rank one, after normalizing the unique nonzero arm vector to squared norm three and writing \(u\) for the squared sum of its coordinates, \(0\le u\le9\), the focal-only stratum has
\[
g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)},
\]
and the comparison-only stratum has
\[
g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},

\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments,
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le2n^{-2}\sup_B
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence \(nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) in \(L^1\) implies first-order plug-in accuracy for both regular rank-two criteria.  The condition \(\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}/n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}\to\infty\) is sufficient. \[

\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.

\[

and let \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\).  For every rank zero, one, or two class \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\),

\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=

\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}

\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le

\]

\[

\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The full-class epsilon selector and the regular rank-two exact argmin are not conflated.

\[

where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree.  Define
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[C]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(C^{\top}\Omega C).
\]
For every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), there is a sequence \(([B_j]_+)_{j\ge1}\subseteq\mathcal B_Z^+\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(S_{B_j})=r_\Omega\) and a projector \(P_\infty\) such that
\[
P_{B_j}\longrightarrow P_\infty,
\qquad P_\infty-P_B\succeq0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}g_{B_j}^+(c_e)\ge g_B^+(c_e)
\quad(e\in\{L,U\}),
\qquad
\limsup_{j\to\infty}w^+(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\]

{"id":"thm:minimax-residual-weak-dominance","kind":"theorem","statement":"Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  On the compact fixed-threshold positive-definite rank-two class \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), the correspondences
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)
\]
are nonempty, the value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\) is attained, and the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate is
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
These are fixed-threshold rank-two objects, distinct from the full-carrier equality correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), which may be empty.  Strict inequality is not universal: if \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\), then \(c_L=c_U=0\), \(Q(0)=0\), and \(w(B)=g_B(0)=0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), so equality holds in the displayed certificate.","free_symbols":["\kappa","\mathcal B_\kappa","\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}","w(B)","B","v_{\mathrm{mm}}","\mathcal A_0","g_B(c)","\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+","F_1","F_0","c_L","c_U","Q(c)"],"depends_on":["ass:exposure-positivity","ass:kappa-feasibility","prop:kappa-exhaustion","def:moment-matrix","def:gain-loss","def:robust-objective","def:argmax-correspondences","lem:ht-affine-drift"],"status":"proved","proof_tex":"\textbf{Proof.}
By ass:kappa-feasibility there is at least one normalized block-separable basis satisfying \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)\ge\kappa\).  Hence \(\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing\).  Proposition prop:kappa-exhaustion shows that \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact and is contained in the positive-definite rank-two ordinary-inverse class \(\mathcal B_Z\).

Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi\) invertible.  On \(\mathcal B_\kappa\),
\[
S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq n\kappa I_2,
\]
so matrix inversion is continuous there.  For each fixed endpoint \(c_e\), \(e\in\{L,U\}\), def:gain-loss therefore makes \(B\mapsto g_B(c_e)\) and \(B\mapsto\ell_B(c_e)\) continuous on normalized representatives.  These maps are invariant under the residual independent sign changes and hence descend continuously to the projective quotient.  Their finite maximum
\[
w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}
\]
is continuous.  The same argument at \(c=0\) makes \(B\mapsto g_B(0)\) continuous.  Equivalently, the endpoint form of \(w\) is also given by lem:ht-affine-drift.  Compactness and the Weierstrass theorem now imply that \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_0\) are both nonempty and that \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) is attained.

Every \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) satisfies \(w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Moreover, for each \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0\), the definition of the global minimum gives
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le w(B_0).
\]
Taking the supremum over the first nonempty correspondence and the infimum over the second yields
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]

The domain distinction is definitional: \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an attained fixed-threshold rank-two argmin, whereas \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\subseteq\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the equality set of a full-carrier infimum and is permitted to be empty.

Finally take \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\).  Both means and variances vanish, both quantile-coupling covariance endpoints equal zero, and def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(0)=0\).  The trace formulas in def:gain-loss then give, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\),
\[
h(0)=g_B(0)=\ell_B(0)=w(B)=0.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\mathcal A_0=\mathcal B_\kappa\), \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=0\), and equality holds.  This supplies the claimed lawful non-strictness witness. \(\square\)"}

Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, this enumeration is nonempty and, for every realized pilot sample,
\[
 \inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k)
 =\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B).

\[

\[
 \widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
 \le
 \inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]

{"id":"def:rank-adaptive-stability-strata","name":"Z,\mathfrak M_{3,n},\mathfrak M_{4,n},s_n,d_n,\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)","construction":"Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
Define the exact covariance-support and dependency-neighborhood quantities
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le j\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{kj}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le j\le N}\#N_{\mathcal G_n}[j].
\]
Whenever \(\mathcal G_n\) is a dependency graph for \(D\), \(s_n\le d_n\).

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).","free_symbols":["n","D","\nu","Z","\Omega","\mathcal G_n","\mathfrak M_{3,n}","\mathfrak M_{4,n}","s_n","d_n","B","b_1","b_0","S_B","\mathcal B_Z^+","\lambda_+(S_B)","\overline a","\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)"],"inputs":["def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain"]}

For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), suppose
\[
[B]_+\in\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda_r,\overline a),
\qquad
\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a},
\]
and define
\[
U_{n,r}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\overline a\,s_n}
{n\lambda_r\pi_{\min,n}^2},
\qquad X_n=\frac{\overline a}{n},
\]
\[

\sqrt{\frac{2s_n}{\lambda_r}},
\qquad
T_{n,r}=\frac1n\{\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}
+\overline a\Gamma_{n,r}\},
\]
\[
R_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}
=4\mathfrak M_{4,n}U_{n,r}^2X_n^2
+4\mathfrak M_{3,n}T_{n,r}U_{n,r}X_n.
\]
Then, for every fixed bounded potential-outcome array,
\[
\left|\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or},+}\mid Y)\right|
\le R_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}.
\]
The oracle variance is exactly
\[

=n^{-2}Y^{\top}\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}Y.
\]
Under ass:iid-potential-pairs,
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or},+}\mid Y)
=\ell_B^+(c_H).
\]

\le\mathbb E_P\!\left[

R_{n,\operatorname{rank}(S_{\widetilde B})}^{\mathrm{ad}}
\right].
\]

For fixed positive lower bounds on \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\) and fixed \(\overline a\), a finite constant \(K_{\mathrm{ad}}\), independent of the selected basis, its positive rank, the bounded array, and \(H\), satisfies

Let \(\mathcal K=\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let \(\mathcal Z\) be the normalized positive-definite rank-two carrier, put \(a(B)=g_B(0)\),
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal K}a(B),
\quad
A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal K}a(B),
\quad
v=\min_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad
A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad
q=\inf_{B\in A_0}w(B).
\]
Fix the finite signed-pivot charts and their semialgebraic quotient distance \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}\).  A primitive geometry record \(\mathscr G_{\mathrm{CAD}}\) consists of exact rational or real-algebraic CAD, KKT, and interval-Hessian certificates with the following components.

First, for some \(\zeta_0,\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}>0\), it certifies the strict inside/outside gaps
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}a(B)
\le a^\star-\zeta_0,
\qquad
\inf_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}w(B)
\ge v+\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}.
\tag{G1}
\]
Second, it gives a finite semialgebraic stratified chart cover of \(A_0\), exact nominal KKT multipliers, linear independence of the active constraint gradients, strictly positive multipliers for active inequalities, and a strictly negative reduced Hessian for the nominal Lagrangian.  On
\[
A_q=\{C\in A_0:w(C)=q\},

Let \(\mathcal K=\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let \(\mathcal Z\) be the normalized positive-definite rank-two carrier, and put \(a(B)=g_B(0)\),
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal K}a(B),
\quad A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal K}a(B),
\quad v=\min_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad q=\min_{B\in A_0}w(B).
\]
Fix the finite signed-pivot charts and their semialgebraic quotient distance \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}\).  A primitive geometry record \(\mathscr G_{\mathrm{CAD}}\) consists only of finite rational or real-algebraic CAD signs, KKT data, derivative bounds, and interval remainders as follows.

First, it certifies numbers \(\zeta_0,\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}a(B)
\le a^\star-\zeta_0,
\qquad
\inf_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}w(B)
\ge v+\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}.
\tag{G1}
\]

Second, it gives a finite semialgebraic stratification \(A_0=\bigcup_j V_j\).  On every signed-pivot chart meeting a stratum \(V_j\), it supplies: exact active constraints; nominal KKT multipliers; linear independence of active gradients; strictly positive multipliers for active inequalities; a certified tubular chart whose derivative splits feasible displacements into directions tangent to \(V_j\), feasible tangent directions transverse to \(V_j\), and active-normal coordinates; lower singular-value bounds for the transverse and normal coordinate map; and interval bounds for its first two derivatives and remainders.  The nominal Lagrangian Hessian is required to be strictly negative only on the feasible tangent directions transverse to \(V_j\), with a certified eigenvalue bounded above by a negative algebraic number.  No curvature is required along \(T_CV_j\), where \(a\) is constant.

Put \(A_q=\{C\in A_0:w(C)=q\}\).  The record certifies a relative semialgebraic neighborhood \(N_q\) of \(A_q\) in \(A_0\).  On every stratum contained in \(N_q\), it supplies exact weights \(\theta_L(C),\theta_U(C)\ge0\), summing to one and supported only on endpoint losses attaining \(w(C)\), and exact KKT normal data proving that the first feasible directional derivative of \(\theta_L(C)\ell_B(c_L)+\theta_U(C)\ell_B(c_U)\) is nonnegative.  It also supplies uniform interval bounds on the endpoint Hessians and Taylor remainders.  On the compact remainder \(A_0\setminus N_q\), it certifies a strictly positive \(w-q\) gap.  These are primitive finite checks; neither quadratic growth nor a global comparison inequality is included in the record.

Third, after the local tube radius is derived from those derivative bounds, CAD certifies on its compact complement constants \(\gamma>0\) and \(R<\infty\) satisfying
\[
a^\star-a(B)\ge\gamma,
\qquad [q-w(B)]_+\le R.
\tag{G2}
\]
Finally, the record contains an exactly feasible algebraic witness \(B_R\in\mathcal K\) and \(\zeta_\Delta>0\) with
\[
w(B_R)\le q-\zeta_\Delta.
\tag{G3}
\]

Every valid \(\mathscr G_{\mathrm{CAD}}\) derives constants \(\rho,\mu>0\) and \(M<\infty\) for
\[
a^\star-a(B)\ge\mu d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)^2,
\qquad
[q-w(B)]_+\le M d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)^2
\quad\text{if }d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)\le\rho,
\tag{G4}
\]
proves
\[
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=A_0,
\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}=A_{\mathrm{mm}},
\qquad q-v\ge\zeta_\Delta>0,
\tag{G5}
\]
and derives the global comparison
\[
[q-w(B)]_+
\le L\{a^\star-a(B)\}
\quad(B\in\mathcal K),
\qquad L=\max\{M/\mu,R/\gamma\}.
\tag{G6}
\]

Consequently, if
\[
e=\sup_{\mathcal K}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|,
\qquad d=\sup_{\mathcal K}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\]
then any empirical nominal maximizer \(\widehat B_0\) and robust minimizer \(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}\) satisfy
\[
w(\widehat B_0)\ge q-2Le,
\qquad w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})\le v+2d.
\]
Define \(V_0\) and \(V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) to be the observable ex ante conditional design-variance performances of these two selected bases.  If
\[
|V_0-w(\widehat B_0)|\le R_0,
\qquad

\quad v=\min_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad q=\min_{B\in A_0}w(B).
\]
Fix the finite signed-pivot charts and their semialgebraic quotient distance \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}\).  A primitive geometry record \(\mathscr G_{\mathrm{CAD}}\) consists only of finite rational or real-algebraic CAD signs, KKT data, derivative bounds, and interval remainders as follows.

First, it certifies numbers \(\zeta_0,\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}a(B)
\le a^\star-\zeta_0,
\qquad
\inf_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}w(B)
\ge v+\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}.
\tag{G1}
\]

Second, it gives a finite semialgebraic stratification \(A_0=\bigcup_j V_j\).  On every signed-pivot chart meeting a stratum \(V_j\), it supplies: exact active constraints; nominal KKT multipliers; linear independence of active gradients; strictly positive multipliers for active inequalities; a certified tubular chart whose derivative splits feasible displacements into directions tangent to \(V_j\), feasible tangent directions transverse to \(V_j\), and active-normal coordinates; lower singular-value bounds for the transverse and normal coordinate map; and interval bounds for its first two derivatives and remainders.  The nominal Lagrangian Hessian is required to be strictly negative only on the feasible tangent directions transverse to \(V_j\), with a certified eigenvalue bounded above by a negative algebraic number.  No curvature is required along \(T_CV_j\), where \(a\) is constant.

Put \(A_q=\{C\in A_0:w(C)=q\}\).  After replacing the finite stratification by a common semialgebraic refinement, the record certifies a relative semialgebraic neighborhood \(N_q\) of \(A_q\) in \(A_0\) that is a union of strata. \]

Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence holds, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where \(C_n\) is exactly the deterministic sensitivity coefficient defined in lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate, and assume along the triangular sequence that
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Put also
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]

\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad

\[

\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]

Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
For the directed local neighborhoods in \(\texttt{ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate}\), retain \(\mathcal G_n=\{(\ell,j):j\in N_\ell\}\) only as a directed relation and define
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{k\ell}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le \ell\le N}\lvert N_\ell\rvert.
\]
No separated-set independence or undirected dependency-graph property is included in these definitions.

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.

\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

Fix displayed constants \(\lambda_{1,n}>0\), \(\lambda_{2,n}>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), and define the stable carrier
\[

=\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{1,n}(\lambda_{1,n},\overline a)
\cup\mathcal S_{2,n}(\lambda_{2,n},\overline a).
\]

\[

=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal K_n^{\mathrm{st}}}w^+(B),
\qquad

\]

changed.from: The causal estimand is the fixed finite-population contrast \(\tau\); the distinct primary ex ante design criterion chooses an armwise-scale projective control span through \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\), where \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-rank block-separable pseudoinverse carrier. For arbitrary real pilot observations, \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}\) is only a classical nonconstructive measurable positive-tolerance selector with no finite stopping rule.  For rational or real-algebraic empirical endpoint input, \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\) finitely certifies an algebraic basis \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}\), its selected rank, positive-eigenvalue isolating intervals, and an \(\varepsilon_m\)-value gap; agreement with the countable selector is not claimed.  Deployment uses \(\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=(D_{i,1}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,1},-D_{i,0}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,0})_{i=1}^n\), \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)=S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and the displayed observable control-variate estimator.  Its oracle variance equals \(\ell_B^+(c_H)\).  The observable bridge is exact at rank zero and has explicit error \(R_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}\) at rank one or two only when the selected-rank event carries a certified lower bound \(\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda_r>0\) and the displayed coordinate envelope.  Its rate is proved from Zhao's directed coordinate-versus-complement neighborhood condition by an explicit multiplicity and directed-cycle enumeration yielding the universal constants \(8\) and \(64\) for the centered third- and fourth-moment moduli; it does not use separated-set dependency-graph independence.  Bounded outcomes, the external unpaired pilot, and selected-rank spectral and coordinate stability remain additional restrictions.
changed.to: The causal estimand remains the fixed finite-population contrast \(\tau\), distinct from the ex ante basis criterion.  The unrestricted benchmark is \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\) on the note's quotient of Zhao's published all-rank pseudoinverse carrier.  For arbitrary real pilots, both the unrestricted and stable positive-tolerance selectors are classical pilot-measurable existence rules without finite stopping tests.
